metadata.title: VERIS → TLCTC Mapping
metadata.description: Maps every VERIS 1.4.1 action variety and vector, action result and attribute outcome enumeration to TLCTC v2.5: the cluster(s) whose generic vulnerability the action exploits (with the rule that decides), the companion step the rules require but VERIS does not record, the boundary context a vector implies, the cause-side partition row for actions that are not threats, and the Data Risk Event code for outcomes.

mapping_types.direct: The value names exactly one generic vulnerability: one cluster.
mapping_types.conditional: The value spans clusters; each target carries the rule and the condition under which it applies. The record alone cannot decide.
mapping_types.chain: The value names one cluster, and the rules require a companion step (before or after) that VERIS does not record.
mapping_types.context: Vectors: no cluster. The value annotates the boundary context, a responsibility-sphere crossing, an intra-system boundary, or a role hint for R-ROLE.
mapping_types.no-cluster: Off the threat axis: the cause-side partition row is named (failure, error_in_use, abuse_of_rights), or the action is intentional but involves no IT-system step (row attack with out_of_scope).
mapping_types.outcome: Not a cause (Axiom III). Attribute values map to a Data Risk Event code; action results map to nothing.
mapping_types.unresolved: Other / Unknown: the record says something happened without saying what. An unresolved step in TLCTC notation, excluded from statistics (R-UNRES-3).

entry_fields.targets[].rule: rule_id from the dictionary that decides the target
entry_fields.targets[].condition: conditional only: when this target applies
entry_fields.targets[].role_hint: server | client: the R-ROLE reading VERIS implies
entry_fields.companion.before / companion.after: chain only: the step the rules require around the named cluster
entry_fields.companion.notation: the sequence in TLCTC notation with placeholders in angle brackets
entry_fields.partition_row: no-cluster only: failure | error_in_use | abuse_of_rights | attack
entry_fields.basis: no-cluster only: the axiom or rule that takes the action off the threat axis
entry_fields.out_of_scope: no-cluster with row attack only: why no cluster applies
entry_fields.dre: outcome only: C | I | Ii | If | A | Av | Ac
entry_fields.certainty: outcome only: potential when the record marks the disclosure as at risk rather than confirmed

entries.veris_description: Disable or interfere with security controls

entries.veris_description: Exploit a misconfiguration (vs vuln or weakness)

entries.veris_description: Use of stolen or default authentication credentials (including credential stuffing)
entries.rationale: Authenticating with a credential that is not the presenter's own is always #4 (R-CRED, Axiom X); the acquisition is a separate earlier step whose cluster VERIS does not record. Default credentials count as stolen for this purpose.

entries.veris_description: Elevation of privilege by another customer in shared environment. Child of 'Exploit vuln'.
entries.rationale: Escaping a tenant boundary exploits a flaw in the shared platform that serves the tenant; the boundary crossed is an intra-system annotation, not a classification input (R-INTRA-7).

entries.veris_description: Virtual machine escape. Child of 'Exploit vuln'.
entries.rationale: The hypervisor serves the guest's requests; a flaw in it is a server-role flaw (R-ROLE, hypercall interface). The |[hypervisor]| boundary is an annotation only (R-INTRA-7).

context.note: channel established by an earlier step

context.note: channel established by an earlier step

entries.rationale: A remote shell is the channel of later steps, not a generic vulnerability; classify the step that provided the shell.

entries.veris_description: Graphical desktop sharing (RDP, VNC, PCAnywhere, Citrix)
entries.rationale: A graphical remote-access service reached from outside; the cluster comes from what was done at it: credential application (#4) or a flaw in the service (#2).

entries.veris_description: Superset of 'Desktop sharing' and '3rd party desktop'.  Please use in place of the other two
entries.rationale: A remote-access service reached from outside; the cluster comes from what was done at it: credential application (#4) or a flaw in the service (#2).
The crossing is an intra-system boundary |[hypervisor][@guest→@host]|; it never changes the cluster (R-INTRA-7), which follows from the flaw exploited (R-ROLE).

entries.veris_description: Penetration of another VM or web site on shared device or infrastructure
entries.rationale: Crossing from one tenant to another is an intra-system or platform boundary annotation; the cluster follows from the flaw or function used to cross it.

entries.veris_description: Network service that is not remote access or a web application.
entries.rationale: A network service in a server role relative to the attacker; the cluster follows from what was exploited at it (#2 for a flaw, #1 for a designed function, #4 for a credential).

entries.veris_description: Partner connection or credential. (Indicates supply chain breach.)
entries.rationale: A partner connection or credential marks a responsibility-sphere crossing ||[…][@Vendor→@Org]||. It is #10 only where a trust artefact from the partner was honoured by the victim's system (R-SUPPLY); otherwise the partner is a transit carrier (⇒) and the step keeps its own cluster.

entries.veris_description: Physical access or connection (i.e., at keyboard or via cable)
entries.rationale: The step was carried out at the keyboard or on a cable; this is the [physical] boundary context of the step, whose cluster follows from what was done (#8 for hardware interaction, #1 or #4 for actions at the console).
A remote-access service in a server role; the cluster follows from what was exploited at it (#4 for credentials, #2 for a flaw in the gateway, #1 for a permissive configuration).
The web application is in a server role relative to the attacker; ambiguous #2 | #3 mappings resolve to #2 here (R-ROLE).
The vector is recorded as unspecified; no context annotation can be derived.
The vector is not recorded; no context annotation can be derived.

entries.veris_description: System or network utilities (e.g., PsTools, Netcat)

targets.condition: the tooling is legitimate software already present or installable through designed functions (living off the land)
the attacker introduced foreign executable content

entries.rationale: System utilities used by an attacker are function abuse unless the binary itself is foreign to the system; VERIS does not record which.
Unwanted advertising code that executes on the system is foreign executable content (#7 at execution, R-EXEC); its delivery is a separate earlier step.

entries.veris_description: Malware creates a backdoor capability for hacking. Child of 'RAT' when combined with 'Trojan'. Child of 'Backdoor or C2'.
entries.rationale: The payload's remote-access capability is a feature of the executed foreign code; #7 is recorded once, at execution (R-EXEC).

entries.veris_description: Malware creates a remote control capability, but it's unclear if it's a backdoor for hacking or C2 for malware. Parent of 'C2' and 'Backdoor'.
entries.rationale: Remote-control capability of the executed foreign code; #7 at execution (R-EXEC), whether the channel is later used by hand or by the malware.
Malware guessing credentials against further systems: the guessing itself is credential application (#4) by the running payload; the payload's execution is the #7 step before it.

entries.veris_description: Malware creates Command and Control capability for malware. Child of 'Backdoor or C2'.
entries.rationale: Command-and-control is a capability of the executed foreign code; #7 at execution (R-EXEC). Later operator actions through the channel classify by their own generic vulnerability.

entries.veris_description: Capture data from application or system process
entries.rationale: Foreign executable content ran on the victim's system: a #7 step is recorded at the execution moment (R-EXEC). The capability VERIS names is a feature of the payload, not a separate step; the step that delivered the payload is a separate earlier step whose cluster VERIS does not record.

entries.veris_description: Capture data stored on system disk
entries.rationale: Foreign executable content ran on the victim's system: a #7 step is recorded at the execution moment (R-EXEC). entries.rationale: Foreign executable content ran on the victim's system: a #7 step is recorded at the execution moment (R-EXEC). entries.rationale: Foreign executable content ran on the victim's system: a #7 step is recorded at the execution moment (R-EXEC). entries.veris_description: Client-side or browser attack (e.g., redirection, XSS, AitB)
entries.rationale: Browser or client attacks (redirection, cross-site scripting, adversary-in-the-browser) exploit a client-role component (R-ROLE); where foreign code then executes, #7 follows (R-EXEC).

entries.veris_description: Cryptocurrency mining, whether or not click fraud. Child of 'Click fraud and cryptocurrency mining'.
entries.rationale: Foreign executable content ran on the victim's system: a #7 step is recorded at the execution moment (R-EXEC). The capability VERIS names is a feature of the payload, not a separate step; the step that delivered the payload is a separate earlier step whose cluster VERIS does not record.
Data-destroying payloads are #7 at execution (R-EXEC); the destruction is the Data Risk Event Av (data absent) on the affected records, never a cluster (Axiom III).
Code that never touches persistent storage is still foreign executable content; #7 is recorded at execution (R-EXEC). Storage location is not a classification input.

companion.after: #5 (interception from the position the payload holds)

entries.rationale: The payload intercepts or relays traffic from the position its execution gave it: #7 at execution (R-EXEC), then #5 for the interception (R-MITM).

entries.veris_description: Malware which compromises a legitimate file rather than creating new filess
entries.rationale: A payload that alters legitimate files is #7 at execution (R-EXEC); the alteration is the Data Risk Event Ii on the affected records (Axiom III).

entries.veris_description: Disable or interfere with security controls
entries.rationale: A payload that disables security controls is #7 at execution (R-EXEC); the disabled control is a control failure, not a threat (Axiom V).

A payload that produces denial of service is #7 at execution on the infected system (R-EXEC); the availability effect is a Data Risk Event (A/Av). Traffic it sends against a third party is #6 in that party's record (R-FLOOD).
A downloader is #7 at its own execution (R-EXEC); the second stage it fetches is a further #7 step when it executes.

entries.veris_description: Exploit a misconfiguration (vs vuln or weakness)
entries.rationale: Malware that uses a permissive configuration exercises a designed function (#1); the payload's own execution is the #7 step it enables (R-EXEC).

entries.veris_description: Modification of the action (rather than the system, as in 'Disable controls') to avoid detection.
entries.rationale: A property of how the payload behaves, not a step: evasion is a capability of the #7 step already recorded.

entries.veris_description: Exploit vulnerability in code (vs misconfig or weakness). This can be used with other malware enumerations, (such as Remote injection when a Remote injection vuln exists.)

targets.condition: the payload exploits a flaw in a server-role component
the payload exploits a flaw in a client-role component

entries.rationale: Malware exploiting a code flaw: the exploitation is #2 or #3 per R-ROLE and enables the #7 execution that follows (R-EXEC); VERIS does not record the role.

entries.veris_description: Export data to another site or system
entries.rationale: Exfiltration capability of the executed foreign code; #7 at execution (R-EXEC), with the Data Risk Event C on the exported records (Axiom III).

companion.after: #5 (interception from the position the payload holds)

entries.rationale: A sniffer captures traffic from the position its execution gave it: #7 at execution (R-EXEC), then #5 for the interception (R-MITM).
Malware presenting captured hashes authenticates as another identity: #4 (R-CRED) performed by the running payload, whose execution is the #7 step before it.
Credential-dumping capability of the executed foreign code; #7 at execution (R-EXEC). Using the dumped credentials is a separate later #4 step (R-CRED).

entries.veris_description: An application which appears legitimate but hides malicious functionality. Child of 'RAT' when combined with 'Backdoor'
entries.rationale: A trojan is foreign executable content that the victim was induced to run: #7 at execution (R-EXEC), typically with #9 as the enabling step.

entries.veris_description: Worm (propagate to other systems or devices)
entries.rationale: A worm is #7 at execution on each host (R-EXEC); its propagation to the next host is a separate step (#2, #3 or #4) followed by a further #7 there.
The record says malware was involved without naming its capability; #7 is likely under R-EXEC but the record does not establish that foreign code executed.
The record says malware was involved without naming its capability; #7 is likely under R-EXEC but the record does not establish that foreign code executed.

entries.veris_description: Malware actions taken through a Command and Control (C2) channel.  Backdoor is only used by hacking.

context.note: channel established by an earlier step

entries.rationale: Actions through an existing command-and-control channel; classify the step that established the channel and each later action by its own generic vulnerability.

entries.veris_description: Directly installed or inserted by threat agent (after system access)
entries.rationale: Installed by the attacker after access was gained: the installation uses designed functions (#1) and the payload's execution is #7, so the sequence is #1 → #7.

entries.veris_description: Downloaded and installed by local malware
entries.rationale: Fetched by malware already running: a #7 → #7 sequence (R-EXEC records each execution).

entries.veris_description: Email. Parent to 'Email attachment', 'Email autoexecute', 'Email link', 'Email unknown'
entries.rationale: Delivered by email: the enabling step is #9 where a person had to act (attachment, link) or #3 where the client executed it unaided (R-ROLE).

entries.veris_description: Email via user-executed attachment. Child of 'Email'
entries.rationale: A user-executed attachment: #9 enables #7 (R-EXEC).

entries.veris_description: Email via automatic execution. Child of 'Email'
entries.rationale: Executed by the mail client without user action: a client-role flaw (#3, R-ROLE) enables #7.

entries.veris_description: Email via embedded link. Child of 'Email'
entries.rationale: A user-followed link: #9 enables the download and #7 at execution (R-EXEC).

entries.veris_description: Email but sub-variety (attachment, autoexecute, link, etc) not known. Child of 'Email'
entries.rationale: Delivered by email, mechanism unknown: the enabler is #9 or #3.

entries.veris_description: Email sub-variety known, but not one of those listed (attachment, link, autoexecute, etc). Child of 'Email'
entries.rationale: Delivered by email through another mechanism: the enabler is #9 or #3.
Delivered over instant messaging: #9 enables #7 where a person had to act.
Reached the host from another infected host: the propagation step is #2, #3 or #4, followed by #7 (R-EXEC).

entries.veris_description: Partner connection or credential. (Indicates supply chain breach.)
entries.rationale: A partner connection or credential marks a responsibility-sphere crossing ||[…][@Vendor→@Org]||. It is #10 only where a trust artefact from the partner was honoured (R-SUPPLY); otherwise the partner is a transit carrier (⇒).

entries.veris_description: Remotely injected by agent (i.e. via SQLi)
entries.rationale: Injected through a server-side flaw (for example SQL injection): #2 enables #7 (R-ROLE, R-EXEC).
Delivered on removable media: [physical] or [human] boundary context; the enabler is #8 (hardware connection) or #9 (a person runs it).

context.note: R-SUPPLY: #10 at the Trust Acceptance Event

entries.rationale: Delivered inside a legitimate update: the Trust Acceptance Event makes this #10 (R-SUPPLY) with the [update] boundary context, followed by #7 at execution.

entries.veris_description: Web application. Parent of 'Web application - download' and 'Web application - drive-by.
entries.rationale: Delivered through a web application: #2 (a flaw in the service) or #9 (a person downloads it) enables #7.

entries.veris_description: Web via user-executed or downloaded content. Child of 'Web application'.
entries.rationale: A user-downloaded file: #9 enables #7 (R-EXEC).

entries.veris_description: Web via auto-executed or "drive-by" infection. Child of 'Web application'.
entries.rationale: Executed by the browser without user action: a client-role flaw (#3, R-ROLE) enables #7.

entries.veris_description: Prepare malicious content in a location where a victim is likely to interact with it. (e.g. SEO - vect: websites, left usbs- vect: removable media, etc)
entries.rationale: A person is induced to interact with prepared content (#9); the payload that then runs is a separate #7 step (R-EXEC).
Recruiting an insider is manipulation of a person (#9); what the insider then does on the system is a separate step (#1, or #4 if they present another identity).

entries.veris_description: Elicitation (subtle extraction of info through conversation)

companion.after: #4 (use of an elicited credential) or a Data Risk Event C

entries.rationale: Extracting information through conversation is #9; where the information is a credential its later use is #4 (R-CRED), where it is data the Data Risk Event C is recorded directly.

entries.veris_description: Modification of the action (rather than the system, as in 'Disable controls') to avoid detection.
entries.rationale: A property of how the manipulation was carried out, not a step.
A demand made to a person is intentional and outside any grant, but it is not a step against an IT system; it belongs to the business-side event chain (BRE), outside the core clusters.

entries.veris_description: Forgery or counterfeiting (fake hardware, software, documents, etc)

targets.condition: a person is deceived by the counterfeit document, hardware or software
a system honours the counterfeit as a trust artefact (Trust Acceptance Event)

entries.rationale: A forgery aimed at a person is #9; a forgery accepted by a system as authoritative is #10 at the Trust Acceptance Event (R-SUPPLY).

entries.veris_description: Influence tactics (Leveraging authority or obligation, framing, etc)
entries.rationale: Authority, obligation or framing used to make a person act (#9); the act they perform on a system is the separate follow-on step, typically #1 (fraudulent transfer through a designed function).

entries.veris_description: Any type of *ishing.  Phishing always involves getting data from the victim. Phishing usually has some element of pretexting, but often it doesn’t rise to the level of an invented scenario. E.g. A fake google login page isn’t really pretexting.
entries.rationale: Phishing obtains data or an action from a person (#9); the credential it harvests is applied in a separate #4 step (R-CRED) and any payload runs as a separate #7 step (R-EXEC).

entries.veris_description: Pretexting (dialogue leveraging invented scenario).  Unlike 'Phishing', does not transfer data. (A fraudulent transfer or changing a bank account on a business account is not really disclosing data.

companion.after: #1 (the action the person performs through a designed function)

entries.rationale: An invented scenario moves a person to act (#9); the action taken through a designed function (payment, account change) is a separate #1 step.

entries.veris_description: Bombarding the user with MFA prompts to get them to accept the login request
entries.rationale: Repeated MFA prompts wear a person down until they approve (#9); the approved login is the attacker authenticating as that person, a separate #4 step (R-CRED).
Disinformation aimed at people is intentional and outside any grant, but it involves no step against the victim's IT system; outside the core clusters.

entries.veris_description: Online scam or hoax (e.g., scareware, 419 scam, auction fraud)
entries.rationale: A hoax moves a person to pay, install or disclose (#9); the follow-on is a separate step (#1 payment through a designed function, #7 installed software, or a Data Risk Event C).

entries.veris_description: Spam (unsolicited or undesired email and advertisements)
entries.rationale: Unsolicited messages are the delivery of a lure to people (#9); the follow-on depends on what the message carried.
The record says a social action occurred without naming it; #9 is likely but the value alone does not establish that a person was manipulated into an IT-system step.

entries.veris_description: Handling of data in an unapproved manner
entries.rationale: Handling data outside the purpose it was entrusted for exceeds the grant even though the access function was available; the action is on the Attack row and uses designed functions (#1, R-SCOPE).

entries.veris_description: Inappropriate use of email or IM
entries.rationale: An insider acting inside the entitlement a grantor conferred, against policy but not against the system: Abuse of Rights, operational risk, no cluster (R-SCOPE).

entries.veris_description: Modification of the action (rather than the system, as in 'Disable controls') to avoid detection.
entries.rationale: A property of how the misuse was carried out, not a step.

entries.veris_description: Storage or distribution of illicit content
entries.rationale: An insider acting inside the entitlement a grantor conferred, against policy but not against the system: Abuse of Rights, operational risk, no cluster (R-SCOPE).

entries.veris_description: Abuse of private or entrusted knowledge
entries.rationale: Using entrusted knowledge for an unauthorised purpose exceeds the grant; where it is applied to a system it is function abuse (#1). Where no IT-system step occurs the event stays outside the core clusters.

entries.veris_description: Inappropriate use of network or Web access including cloud services
entries.rationale: An insider acting inside the entitlement a grantor conferred, against policy but not against the system: Abuse of Rights, operational risk, no cluster (R-SCOPE).

entries.veris_description: Sharing of a legitimate user's credential or session

companion.before: the sharer's act (Abuse of Rights, operational risk, no cluster)

entries.rationale: The person who uses a shared credential authenticates as an identity that is not their own: #4 (R-CRED). The sharing itself is an in-grant policy violation with no cluster (R-SCOPE).

entries.veris_description: Abuse of physical access to asset
entries.rationale: Abusing physical access one is entitled to, for a purpose outside the grant, is function abuse at the console (#1); it is #8 only where hardware itself is manipulated.

Using system privileges for a purpose outside the grant is the definition of Abuse of Functions (#1): the access was designed, the use was not. 'Functioned as designed' does not make the action in-grant (R-SCOPE).

entries.veris_description: Actor photographs the confidentiality data variety.
entries.rationale: Photographing displayed data exceeds the purpose for which the display function was granted; the display is the abused function (#1), and the Data Risk Event C follows.

entries.veris_description: Assault (threats or acts of physical violence)
entries.rationale: Violence or threats against a person are intentional and outside any grant, but they are not a step against an IT system; outside the core clusters.
Getting past a physical barrier exploits the physical layer's lack of control over access to the substrate (#8, mechanical vector).
Attaching a device to hardware or a port is direct physical interaction with the substrate (#8); if the device then runs code on the system, #7 follows (R-EXEC).
Deliberately damaging hardware acts on the substrate itself (#8); the availability effect is the Data Risk Event Av.
Disabling a physical barrier or sensor acts on the substrate (#8).

entries.veris_description: Modification of the action (rather than the system, as in 'Disable controls') to avoid detection.
entries.rationale: A property of how the physical step was carried out, not a step.
Installing a skimming device is a mechanical interaction with the terminal (#8); the device then captures the channel at the physical interface.

entries.veris_description: Snooping (sneak about to gain info or access)
entries.rationale: Sneaking about to observe or reach systems exploits the physical layer's lack of control over who is present (#8, signal vector: observation). Observation of people with no system involved is outside core.
Monitoring systems or screens exploits emanations and line of sight, a physical-layer property (#8, signal vector). Surveillance of people with no system involved is outside core.
Altering hardware's form or function acts on the substrate (#8); a hardware implant that runs code adds #7 (R-EXEC).
Taking an asset exploits the physical layer's lack of control over possession (#8); the Data Risk Event follows from what the asset held.
A physical tap on a line exploits a physical-layer property of the substrate (#8, signal vector); the interception it enables is #5 once the position exists (R-MITM).

No disclosure: no Data Risk Event on the confidentiality property.
Data was at risk but disclosure is not confirmed: recorded as a potential Data Risk Event C.
Confirmed disclosure to a party not entitled to the data: Data Risk Event C.
Disclosure status not recorded: no Data Risk Event can be asserted.
A change in a person's behaviour is not a change in a record's state; no Data Risk Event.
A record (the account store) now holds content that its authorised process did not produce: Ii.
Content was replaced: the record's correspondence to its intended state failed: Ii.
The transaction record is accurate about what happened but misattributed to an entitled party: If.
The physical state of the asset no longer corresponds to its intended state: Ii.
Log content no longer corresponds to what occurred: Ii.

entries.rationale: Authenticity failed: content may be accurate but its attribution is false: If.
